findings.reason: the section's whole premise is that the run writes thousands of names and needs a recovery point, and as written a node can certify a checkpoint whose restart silently lost nodes, which is the failure the checkpoint exists to prevent.
findings.text: §3's final clause requires only that "the graph is back up and answers a read afterwards", so a restart that comes up with a truncated store passes: the repository's own checkpoint criterion in imas_codex/graph/AGENTS.md ("Checkpointing the graph") is that the live read after the restart "return[s] the same node count as before", and §3's weaker wording drops exactly the comparison that would catch a bad restore

findings.reason: §4 states this branch is the expected close, so the branch most likely to be exercised is the one with a silent-omission hole, and the repair is the same per-source listing the earlier review rounds already forced at class level.
findings.text: the cost-limit branch closes on "every source run has its outcome recorded, each class left unrun is listed with its source count", which leaves a class entered and then abandoned by the cost limit satisfying neither condition: the sources it never reached were not run (so carry no outcome) and the class was not left unrun (so is not listed), letting up to a whole partially-run class disappear from the accounting; the census's per-class band (USD 50.68–101.27 across the six classes against a USD 145.76 ceiling) makes a stop inside the 395-source below-floor class the likely shape of this close
